metadata.title: Sampling Distribution of the Mean
metadata.subject: Statistics
metadata.objective: Show sample means varying around the population mean and their spread shrinking as n grows.
misconceptions: A larger sample makes each observation closer to the mean
The sampling distribution is the population distribution
expectedUnderstanding: Individual observations keep the population spread.
Sample means center near the population mean.
The spread of sample means decreases as n increases, roughly as sigma divided by the square root of n.
The sampling distribution of the mean is not the population distribution.

primitives.text: Sampling Distribution of the Sample Mean
Sample means x-bar (center near mu; spread shrinks with n)

checkpoints.title: Two distributions
checkpoints.body: Top: individual values, spread wide across the population. Bottom: sample means. The orange line marks the population mean, and the means sit around it.

checkpoints.title: Change n
checkpoints.body: Increase n and the sample means cluster more tightly. Standard error is sigma divided by the square root of n. Individual observations do not move closer to the mean; only the spread of the means shrinks.

checkpoints.title: Keep them distinct
checkpoints.body: A sample mean is an average of n observations. The sampling distribution is the distribution of those averages, not the population distribution.

narration.text: The top row shows individual values from a population. They stay spread out. The bottom row shows sample means, centered near the population mean.
As the sample size grows, the sample means cluster more tightly. The standard error is sigma divided by the square root of n. A larger sample does not pull each observation closer to the mean.
Keep the two distributions separate. The sampling distribution describes sample means, not individual observations, so it is not the population distribution.

fallback.text: Individual observations keep the population spread. Sample means center near the population mean. As sample size n grows, the standard error sigma divided by the square root of n shrinks, so the sample means cluster more tightly. A larger n does not make each observation closer to the mean, and the sampling distribution of the mean is not the population distribution.

accessibility.alt: Top strip: five individual observations spread widely around a center line. Bottom strip: four sample means clustered near the same center. A sample-size slider from 4 to 64 makes the sample means move closer together while the individual observations stay spread out.
